newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy seen issuing 12 trln lire Btps/CCTs.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy seen issuing 12 trln lire Btps/CCTs.

text.p: The Italian Treasury is expected to issue 9.0 to 12 trillion lire ($7.3 billion) of fixed-rate government bonds (BTPs) and floating-rate certificates (CCTs) at its mid-month auction, analysts polled by Reuters said on Friday.
They expect an average 10.5 trillion lire of paper will be issued at the auctions on February 13 and 14.
Some six trillion lire of CCTs mature on February 18, and the Treasury said on Thursday it will issue the fifth tranche of January 1, 2004 CCTs bearing a 3.45-percent coupon at those auctions.

It will also issue a new February 15, 2000 BTP with a 6.25-percent coupon and a third tranche of a January 1, 2007 BTP bearing a 6.25-percent coupon. It will also reopen a November 1, 2026 30-year BTP with a 7.25-percent coupon.
Amounts on offer will be announced on February 10.

According to one analyst, the decision to issue a new three-year CCT is due to the Treasury's attempt to avoid too many bills maturing by the same date. "When the Treasury issued the Janaury 1, 2000 BTP, there were already a lot of bills maturing," the analyst said.
